defects.rule: scratch: width_mm 0.88 >= 0.5 -> critical => HOLD_FOR_QA
defects.action: 1. Do not paint over it. 2. QA checks the depth with a gauge. On 3-8 mm plate up to 0.2 mm deep may stay; 0.2-0.4 mm only if the affected area is 5 % or less; deeper must be repaired. 3. If it runs into an edge or hole, QA decides on repair or scrap.
notes: depth not measured, operator check with a gauge

defects.rule: scratch: width_mm 0.08 < 0.2, length_mm 14.35 < 25 -> minor => PASS
defects.action: 1. Logged as an imperfection; no repair needed. 2. Keep the part in the normal flow.

defects.rule: corrosion: area_pct 0.1 < 1 -> minor; estimated rust grade A (visual analogue); confidence 0.43 < 0.5: uncertain, operator to confirm -> HOLD_FOR_QA => HOLD_FOR_QA
defects.reference: ISO 8501-1 / IS 9954 (rust grades A-D); ISO 4628-3 bands (1 % / 8 %)
defects.action: 1. Uncertain detection: look at the marked spot and run a fingernail across it. 2. If the mark is real, QA applies the rule shown; if not, QA logs a false call. Rule action: 1. Clean the rust spot locally with a wire brush or power tool to St 3. 2. Inspect again before painting.

references.text: On 3-8 mm plate, imperfections up to 0.2 mm deep may stay, any number of them.

references.id: EN 10163-2 / ISO 7788 Table 2 (3-8 mm: 0.4 mm, <= 5 % area)
references.text: On 3-8 mm plate, discontinuities up to 0.4 mm deep may stay unrepaired if they affect 5 % of the surface or less.
Rust grades A to D describe mill-scale state and visible pitting; preparation grades are St 2 / St 3 by hand or power tool and Sa 1 to Sa 3 by blasting.
Rusted-area degrees near 1 % and 8 % of the surface, borrowed as area-band edges (the scale itself is for painted steel).
